The charge sheet has been filed in this case by the Police Inspector of Basavanagudi Women police station against the accused no.1 and 2 for the alleged offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504 Hindu P vs Satish Babu on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31561277/
1 and 506 of IPC and Sec.4 of D.P.Act.
2.

In briefly the case of the prosecution is as follows:-
It is the case of the prosecution that the accused no.1 married C.W.1-.Hindu.P on 21.10.2019 as per Hindu rites and customs and after marriage while C.W.1 was residing with the accused No.1 at the matrimonial home, the accused No.1 with an intention to get additional dowry demanded C.W.1 to money for opening a medical shop and as such C.W.1 took a loan of Rs.3,00,000/- and the father of C.W.1 also gave Rs.1,00,000/- to the accused no.1 and later on the accused no.1 without the knowledsge of C.W.1 pledged her gold jewelry and took Rs.3,00,000/- and when C.W.1 asked the accused no.1 for the gold jewelry, he picked up quarrel with C.W.1 abused C.W.1 in filthy language knowingly that It would give provocation to C.W.1 to breach public peace and harassed C.W.1 physically and mentally and threatened C.W.1 to do away with her life.
Therefore the C.W.1 lodged the complaint against accused no.1 and 2 before the Basavanagudi Women Police seeking necessary action against them in accordance with law.
3. On the basis of the said complaint given by C.W.1, the complainant police have registered the case under Crime No1361/2022 and sent FIR to this Court and to their concerned higher authorities.

Thereafter, the complainant police have visited the spot and conducted the spot C.C.8367/2023 mahazar in the presence of the panch witnesses, herein after recorded the statements of witnesses who availed in the station subsequently who availed where the said mahazars have been drawn,
after completion of the investigation the IO has arived at a conclusion that there are sufficient materials as to prosecute the accused no.1 and 2 , for which charge sheet has been filed for the above said offences.

4. After filing of the charge sheet, this Court registered the case is as numbered above, before that the accused persons were enlarged on bail in Crl.Misc.547/2023, subsequently in persuance of summons the accused no.1 and 2 appeared before this Court and were enlarged on bail, meanwhile copies of the charge sheet and other prosecution papers were duly supplied as required under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.
Accused no.2 is reported to be dead, as such case against accused no.2 is abated and proceeded only against accused no.1.

After hearing both sides, this court found that there were sufficient reasons so as to frame charge against the accused no.1, therefore charge was framed and read over and explained to the accused No.1 in the language known to him, after understanding the same he denied the same and claimed to be tried, accordingly, proceeded with trial.
5. In order to prove its case, the prosecution has examined one witness who is said to be victim as P.W.1 and got marked two documents at Ex.P-1 and 2.

As there are no any incriminating materials forth coming against the accused, as to which summoning of remaining witnesses would no purpose to serve and therefore CW-2 to 8 ordered to be given up by rejecting the submission made by the learned PP.
Consequently, recording of statement of accused as required under section 313 of Cr.P.C also dispensed with.

7. In view of above said facts and circumstances the following points that would arise for my consideration are as follows:-
POINTS FOR CONSIDERATION 1.

Whether the prosecution further proves beyond all reasonable doubt the accused no.1 married C.W.1-.Hindu.P on 21.10.2019 as per Hindu rites and customs and after marriage while C.W.1 was residing with the accused No.1 at the matrimonial home,
the accused No.1 with an intention to get additional dowry demanded C.W.1 to money for opening a medical shop and as such C.W.1 took a loan of Rs.3,00,000/-
and the father of C.W.1 also gave Rs.1,00,000/- to the accused no.1 and later on the accused no.1 without the knowledsge of C.W.1 pledged her gold jewelry and took Rs.3,00,000/- and thereby the accused no.1 and 2 committed the offence punishable U/Sec. 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act?

2. Whether the prosecution further proves beyond all reasonable doubt that after marriage while C.W.1 was residing with the accused no.1 and 2 at Bengaluru, accused no.1 lost his job and was living on the earnings of C.W.1 and the accused no.1 demanded C.W.1 to give money for opening a medical shop and as such C.W.1 took a loan of Rs.3,00,000/- and the father of C.W.1 also gave Rs.1,00,000/- to accused no.1, and later on accused no.1 without the knowledge of C.W.1 pledged her gold jewelry and took Rs.3,00,000/-
and when C.W.1 asked accused no.1 for the gold jewelry the accused no.1 picked up quarrel with C.W.1 and thereby the accused subjected C.W.1 to cruelty and thereby committed the offence of subjecting C.W.1 to cruelty and thereby the accused no.1 and 2 have committed an offence C.C.8367/2023 punishable under section 498A r/w Sec. 34 of IPC?
3. Whether the prosecution further proves beyond all reasonable doubt that while the C.W.1 was residing at the matrimonial house the accused no.1 and 2 with an intention to commit an offence and in furtherance of their common intention, abused C.W.1 in filthy language knowingly that it would give provocation to C.W.1 to breach public peace and thereby the accused committed the offence of "intentional insult" punishable U/s 504 r/w Sec. 34 of IPC?
4. Whether the prosecution further proves beyond all reasonable doubt that during the period when C.W.1 was staying at the matrimonial house, the accused no.1 and 2 criminally intimidated to the life of C.W1 and thereby the accused have committed an offence of "criminal intimidation" punishable U/s 506 r/w Sec.34 of IPC?

8. My answers to the above points are as under:
Point Nos.1 to 4: In the 'Negative' Point No.5: As per the final order, for the following:-
REASONS 9. Point No.1 to 4 : These points are taken up together for common discussion in order to avoid the repetation of facts.
10. In order to prove its case, the prosecution has examined the complainant/C.W.1 as P.W.1 and got marked two documents on her behalf as Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2.

The C.W.1 being complainant as well as victim in this case is examined as P.W.1 and Ex.P.1 and 2 documents got C.C.8367/2023 marked on her behalf, as far as appreciation of oral and documentary evidence is concerned P.W.1 is the complainant by name Indu.P
and she deposed in her evidence that accused No.1 is her ex-husband and they are divorced.
She further deposed that her marriage was solemnized with the accused No.1 on 21.10.2019 at Bengaluru.

Further she deposed that after her marriage with the accused No.1 she was residing at the matrimonial house with the accused and they were living with together in cordial terms and the accused persons did not extend any physical and mental harassment towards her.
She further deposed that she deposed that she has not lodged complaint against the accused persons.

She deposed that when she had been to Basavanagudi Women P.S in the year 2022 police took her signatures on two documents and she does not know the contents of Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 and police did not draw any mahazar before her presence as per Ex.P.2.

She identified her signature on Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 but she pleaded ignorance about the contents of Ex.P-1 and 2 as to which when learned Assistant Public Prosecutor treated this witness as hostile and with the permission of the court,
cross-examined her even in that process also learned A.P.P. failed to elicit anything from her mouth.

11. As the first informant/complainant P.W.1 being the material witness in this case has not supported the case of the prosecution and as she turned hostile by giving a complete go-bye statement, due to which other prosecution witness were given up, as it would serve no purpose to summon the other witnesses, during the course of prosecution evidence two documents got marked as Ex.P1 and P.2.
So far as Ex.P1 is the complaint and Ex.P.2 is the spot mahazar, but the prosecution witness did not support the contents which are mentioned C.C.8367/2023 in the same

,
therefore whatever the suspicious circumstances pleaded while framing of charge remained as same.

On considering these facts herein no incriminating materials forthcoming against the accused persons and the prosecution has not established the ingredients of the alleged offences against the accused no.1

however herein no positive evidence to prove the guilt of the accused no.1 , for which this Court is of the considered opinion that prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused no.1 beyond all reasonable doubt.
Hence, benefit of doubt goes to the accused no.1, for which I answer point Nos.1 to 4 in the 'Negative'.

sentences.text:
In view of my findings on point Nos.1 to 4 and reasons assigned therein, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
Acting under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C., the accused no.1 is not found guilty and he is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Secs.498A, 504 and 506 of IPC and Sec.4 of D.P.Act.
The bail bond executed by the accused No.1 stands cancelled.

In compliance of section 437-A of Cr.P.C. the bail bond executed by the accused no.1 is ordered to be continued in force for six months or till issuance of notice in respect of any appeal [if C.C.8367/2023 preferred] against the present Judgment before the Appellate Court.
(Dictated to the Stenographer, transcript revised, corrected and signed & then pronounced in the Open court on this the 03rd day of June, 2025.)

(KESHAVA.K)
